summary: Test-only fixture fix in tests/test_mac_method88.py (no production changes). Root causes: (1) ShellMockSerial._rewrite tried line.lstrip().startswith('dmesg'), but every framed serial line is prefixed with the production marker/begin framing, so the inner dmesg never matched; the real host dmesg then ran unprivileged and _capture_state raised 'dmesg.before exit=1', which cascaded into test_full_88_two_role2_boots (ERROR), test_unchanged_boot_id_stops_before_boot_two_cases (only 1 flash) and test_technical_case_failure_is_not_retried (no archive produced). Fix: stop rewriting the framed body and instead inject a real dmesg() shell function (and a portable base64() function for `base64 FILE` on hosts without GNU coreutils) into the same /bin/sh that runs the framed command, so the production capture gate still executes for real. (2) build_package returns 3 values but the second/tamper test unpacked 2 -> unpack the middle with `_`. (3) The added meta check compared against runner.boots[...]['kernel_release'], but the capture returns uname_r -> compare against ['uname_r']. Framework/assertions untouched (88 cases, 2 role2 flashes, differing boot ids, stop/retry/archive/metadata checks all preserved); original echo of the framed command is unchanged. Please re-run the 26 tests to confirm 0 errors/0 failures (I cannot execute tests).

_SHA256_CMD = _sha256_command()

# Stand-in shell builtins injected ahead of every framed command.  They live in
# the same /bin/sh that executes the framed body, so the production capture
# gate still runs for real while ``dmesg`` and ``base64 FILE`` keep working on
# an unprivileged host and on hosts without GNU coreutils (BSD/macOS base64
# takes an input file via stdin redirection, not a positional argument).
SHELL_PRELUDE = (
    "dmesg() { echo mock-dmesg; }\n"
    "base64() { command base64 < \"$1\"; }\n"
)

DUMMY_ROLE2_BIT_SHA256 = hashlib.sha256(b'role2-bit-payload').hexdigest()
